newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil settles mixed, soymeal finishes higher.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil settles mixed, soymeal finishes higher.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended mostly lower Tuesday on commercial selling, and soymeal ended higher, floor traders said.
On the day in soyoil trade, ADM sold 200 lots May and 100 July, Cargill sold 100 July, and Produce Grain sold 100 July and 200 May, pit sources said.
Some traders also viewed the soyoil market as technically weak following several session of sharp gains.
"The (soy)oil market is just settling back in a little bit of corrective action after all those rallies we've had," a pit trader said.
Soymeal futures found support from profit taking on the soyoil/soymeal spread. Near the open, May soymeal fell as much as $3.00 per ton before ending with gains.
Talk that China was looking to buy an unspecified quantity of South American soymeal was said to limit gains in CBOT futures, traders said.
CBOT soymeal settled up $0.60 to $2.60 per ton, with July up $2.60 at $270.40. Soyoil ended up 0.05 cent a lb to down 0.20 cent, with July down 0.04 at 25.05 cents.
U.S. exporters could offer no confirmation of the deal, but one CBOT trader with strong links to the export markets said there were some "very big trades" on the way.
In soymeal trade Merrill Lynch bought 500 lots of July and Smith Barney and Dean Witter each bought 200 lots July. Refco sold 300 lots July, and Griffin Trading sold 300 lots July, pit traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by the CBOT at 15,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 23,856 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 19,000 lots, against Monday's 24,226.
